findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` to the Scope section and update `test_p9_not_applicable_for_container` (and add a sibling `test_p9_advisory_on_poisoned_container` case) to match the new behavior where a container with a non-closed, impact-less child yields an advisory rather than a clean pass.
evidence: test_p9_not_applicable_for_container asserts `r.status == 'pass' and r.coverage['applicable'] is False` for a story with children
Plan Scope lists only `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py` for test changes

Plan states P9 will 'Surface an ADVISORY (never blocking) on a container whose inheritance is poisoned' — this changes P9 behavior for the poisoned-container case that the unit test currently covers with a clean pass
findings.finding: The plan's scope omits `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`, which contains existing P9 unit tests that directly call `p9_file_impact_coverage` and assert the OLD behavior: `test_p9_not_applicable_for_container` (line 746–750) asserts `status == 'pass'` and `coverage['applicable'] is False` for any container. After the plan's extension adds an advisory for containers with poisoned inheritance (non-closed child with empty file_impact), this test asserts the pre-change behavior and will fail.
scenarios: make test runs `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` as part of the default non-integration suite; `test_p9_not_applicable_for_container` fails because the container with an impact-less child now returns an advisory instead of a clean pass, breaking AC8 ('the default non-integration pytest suite exits zero')
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope section add `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`. Update `test_p9_not_applicable_for_container` to cover only the effective-inheritance case (all children have file_impact), and add `test_p9_advisory_on_poisoned_container` asserting `status == 'fail'` (advisory) and the offending child id(s) appear in the finding when at least one non-closed child has empty file_impact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in the Approach that ANY child `file_impact` read failure (not just all-children failure) triggers the whole-batch fail-closed fallback (whole-HEAD), so a single unreadable child cannot silently shrink the signed dependency set.
evidence: 'Read failures keep the pre-change behavior (fail-closed to whole-HEAD), logged' — does not distinguish single-child failure from all-children failure
If a single child read failure is silently ignored (child excluded from union), the signed dep set is smaller than the true scope, creating a fail-open window for that child's files
Poison rule is defined only for empty file_impact, not for unreadable file_impact
findings.finding: The error-handling policy for child `file_impact` read failures does not specify per-child vs. whole-batch semantics: if one child's read fails, it is unclear whether only that child is treated as 'poisoned' (fail-closed, union aborted) or whether the remaining children's declared impacts are still included in the union. A fail-open interpretation (skip the failed child, keep others) would silently undercount the dependency set for that container.
findings.location: Approach step 1: 'Read failures keep the pre-change behavior (fail-closed to whole-HEAD), logged.'
scenarios: A transient store error on one child's file_impact read causes that child to be silently excluded from the union; the container's attestation covers fewer files than it should; a change to that child's file is not caught by drift detection.
A systematic store degradation causes all child reads to fail; behavior (whole-HEAD fallback) is correct here, but the single-failure case is still ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach step 1: 'A read failure for any individual child is treated identically to that child having an empty file_impact: the poison rule fires and the entire union falls back to the pre-change (whole-HEAD) set, logged with the failing child id.'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete closed-status predicate in Approach step 1 — either name the specific status values that count as 'closed' (e.g., 'status in {Done, Closed}') or explicitly delegate to a named shared helper (e.g., 'use the same `is_closed(ticket)` predicate that `attest.current_material_fingerprint` uses internally').
evidence: "Child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads `attest.current_material_fingerprint` uses"
Absence: no statement of which status value(s) constitute 'closed', no named predicate (e.g., `is_closed()`)
The AC fixture for AC3 ('one closed impact-less child') requires the implementation to evaluate closed-ness but the plan provides no criterion for that evaluation
findings.finding: The plan directs the executor to read child 'statuses' from the same light-store reads as `attest.current_material_fingerprint`, but never states which concrete status value(s) (e.g., 'Done', 'Closed', 'Won't Do') satisfy the 'closed child' predicate that gates the poison rule and the 'closed children neither contribute nor poison' rule. An executor implementing the status check must infer the closed-status definition from reading the existing function rather than from the plan.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('Closed children neither contribute files nor poison'); AC3 ('Closed children neither contribute paths nor poison the union')
scenarios: Executor implements status check using a status string that differs from the existing predicate, causing closed children to be incorrectly treated as open (poisoning the union) or vice versa.
A future status rename in the store silently breaks the closed-child exclusion because the implementation was guessed rather than delegated to a shared predicate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Approach step 1: 'Evaluate closed-ness using the same `is_closed()` helper (or equivalent predicate) that `attest.current_material_fingerprint` already applies to child ids, so status-vocabulary changes propagate to both sites automatically.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an Acceptance Criterion asserting that when a child's file_impact read fails, the signed manifest's dep set is unchanged from pre-change behavior (empty → whole-HEAD fallback applies), verified by a test that injects a read error into the child store lookup.
evidence: 'Read failures keep the pre-change behavior (fail-closed to whole-HEAD), logged.' — Approach step 1
No AC in the eight listed criteria mentions read failures, error handling, or logging behavior.
findings.finding: Approach step 1 describes a read-failure behavior ('Read failures keep the pre-change behavior (fail-closed to whole-HEAD), logged') as a deliverable, but no Acceptance Criterion verifies it — there is no AC asserting that a simulated child file_impact read failure leaves the manifest's dep set unchanged (whole-HEAD fallback) rather than inheriting a partial union or raising an exception.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (read-failure behavior) vs Acceptance Criteria (no covering AC)
scenarios: A child ticket's file_impact lookup throws a network/store error at review time; the implementation inherits a partial union (fail-open) instead of falling back to whole-HEAD, and no test catches this regression.
A future refactor removes the read-failure guard; no AC fails, so the regression ships.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: '[ ] Read failure on any child file_impact lookup: the signed dep set is unchanged (empty → whole-HEAD fallback); a simulated store error in an interface test confirms the claim is not blocked by unrelated commits and the failure is logged.' Map this to the existing test file.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `dependency_hashes` should accept an optional `children` parameter (pre-assembled from `PlanContext.children`) to avoid re-reading child state that `assemble_context` already fetched, or explicitly document that independent reads are intentional to keep the resign path consistent.
evidence: orchestrator.py:207 `try:  # fetch full child state (deps + file_impact) for P5/P8` — each child's show_ticket result, including file_impact, is already in ctx.children
manifest.py:241-260: `dependency_hashes` currently has no PlanContext or children parameter — the plan adds child reads internally

The plan states: 'child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads `attest.current_material_fingerprint` uses' — but current_material_fingerprint (attest.py:769) itself does a fresh list_tickets, independent of any cached PlanContext
ABSENCE: the Approach and Scope sections name no parameter change to `dependency_hashes` signature to accept pre-assembled children
findings.finding: The proposed `dependency_hashes` extension re-reads child ids, statuses, and `file_impact` via independent store calls (`_reads.list_tickets` + `rebar.get_file_impact` per child) — but on the primary `review_plan` path this data is already fully assembled in `PlanContext.children` (each child was fetched via `show_ticket` in `_assemble_context_uncached`, which includes `file_impact`). The plan does not mention passing the assembled children to `dependency_hashes` or acknowledge the duplication.
scenarios: On the `review_plan` path, `assemble_context` already paid the N+1 read cost; `dependency_hashes` would repeat it — bounded duplication on every container review.
On the `resign_plan_review` path no PlanContext is available, so independent reads are necessary — meaning the design must consciously choose between two call patterns or unify them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a sequencing note in the Testing section (and optionally a pytest skip marker or fixture guard in the named test file) stating that the claim-gate interface tests require 72d9-8fbd to be merged first, consistent with the Context dependency declaration.
evidence: 'Depends on 72d9-8fbd (athletic-esthetical-polecat) landing first: before that fix, scoped dependency sets are inert in attested mode, so giving containers a non-empty set would move them OFF the only working invalidation (whole-HEAD) onto a broken path.'
Testing section describes claim-gate assertions with no mention of skip markers, ordering guards, or conditional execution relative to 72d9-8fbd.
findings.finding: The Context section states a hard sequencing dependency on ticket 72d9-8fbd ('before that fix, scoped dependency sets are inert in attested mode, so giving containers a non-empty set would move them OFF the only working invalidation onto a broken path'), yet the Testing section describes interface tests asserting claim-gate outcomes (unrelated commit keeps claim open; child-declared-file commit blocks claim) with no conditional guard, skip marker, or ordering note — so if those tests run before 72d9-8fbd merges they would exercise the broken (inert scoped dep) code path and either pass vacuously or fail for the wrong reason, giving false signal.
findings.location: Context ('Depends on 72d9-8fbd landing first') vs Testing section (unconditional interface test description)
scenarios: CI runs this ticket's tests before 72d9-8fbd merges; tests either spuriously pass (inert dep set means whole-HEAD invalidation still fires, making the 'unrelated commit keeps claim open' assertion fail) or give misleading results.
A developer implements the changes in isolation and cannot verify the interface tests until the dependency lands, with no documented expectation.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section add: 'These interface tests require 72d9-8fbd to have landed; mark them with @pytest.mark.depends_on("72d9-8fbd") or place them in a dedicated suite skipped until that ticket merges.' Also add a one-line note in tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py's fixture or module docstring referencing the dependency.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in the AC or a terminology note whether 'rebar.claim' and 'claim_gate_check' are the same API call or different entry points, and use consistent naming across AC #4 and AC #5 (or briefly define both).
evidence: AC #4: '...both asserted via rebar.claim.'
AC #5: '...asserted via claim_gate_check.'
No definition or distinction between rebar.claim and claim_gate_check appears elsewhere in the plan.
findings.finding: AC #4 uses 'rebar.claim' and AC #5 uses 'claim_gate_check' as the verification mechanism without explaining whether these are the same API, different entry points, or distinct abstractions — creating ambiguous terminology that could cause the implementer to target different code surfaces for each assertion.
findings.location: AC #4 ('asserted via rebar.claim') vs AC #5 ('asserted via claim_gate_check')
scenarios: Implementer writes AC #5's test against rebar.claim (assuming they're the same), missing a distinct claim_gate_check code path that has different behavior for pin/material drift.
Reviewer cannot determine whether the two ACs are testing the same gate at different layers or genuinely different APIs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the child file_impact read and child material-fingerprint read in `dependency_hashes` are taken from the same atomic snapshot (e.g., a single light-store transaction or a local snapshot captured once at the start of the function) to prevent a concurrent child update from producing an internally inconsistent signed manifest.
evidence: 'Child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads `attest.current_material_fingerprint` uses; child file_impact via `rebar.get_file_impact`.' — two separate reads from shared mutable store, no atomicity guarantee stated.
The plan specifies read-failure handling but not concurrent-write handling during the review window.
The plan's self-healing mechanism (pin/material drift invalidation) only activates on the NEXT claim check, not at manifest-signing time — so a brief inconsistent manifest is possible.
findings.finding: The plan does not specify that the child file_impact read (used to build the union in `dependency_hashes`) and the child material-fingerprint pinning (used by `attest.current_material_fingerprint`) are performed atomically or from the same consistent snapshot of the light store. A concurrent child update — e.g., a child's file_impact being updated mid-container-review — could cause the signed manifest to embed a union computed from the new file_impact while the pinned fingerprint still reflects the old child state (or vice versa), producing an internally inconsistent manifest that neither correctly reflects the pre-change nor the post-change child scope.
findings.location: Approach §1: 'Child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads `attest.current_material_fingerprint` uses; child file_impact via `rebar.get_file_impact`.'
scenarios: CI parallel workflow: two sibling child-ticket reviews and a container review run concurrently; a child's file_impact is committed between the container's `get_file_impact` call and its `material_fingerprint` pin call; the resulting container manifest encodes a union that does not match any internally consistent state of the child, causing claim-gate to block the container on drift immediately after signing — a spurious gate failure requiring a re-review within the same CI run.
findings.suggested_fix: At the start of `dependency_hashes`, capture a single snapshot of each direct child's (id, status, file_impact, material_fingerprint) in one light-store read (or under a read lock if the store supports it), then use only that snapshot for both the union computation and the fingerprint pinning — eliminating the TOCTOU window between the two reads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or a runtime guard in the implementation) that verifies or enforces the 72d9-8fbd sequencing dependency before the scoped inheritance path is activated — e.g., an integration test that asserts claim blocking still works when the dependency is absent, or a feature-flag/version check in dependency_hashes that falls back to whole-HEAD when the underlying scoped-dep support is not present.
evidence: 'before that fix, scoped dependency sets are inert in attested mode, so giving containers a non-empty set would move them OFF the only working invalidation (whole-HEAD) onto a broken path'
Absence: no AC verifies or guards that 72d9-8fbd has merged before the inheritance path is activated
E3(d): the plan changes behavior for all containers but does not acknowledge or protect against the caller-breaking scenario it itself identifies
findings.finding: The plan explicitly acknowledges that enabling scoped inheritance before ticket 72d9-8fbd lands would move containers OFF the only working invalidation path (whole-HEAD) onto a broken one, but provides no AC, guard, or implementation mechanism to enforce or verify this ordering. An agent building this plan in isolation could introduce the inheritance path into a system where scoped dependency sets are inert, silently degrading container attestation integrity.
findings.location: Context section ('Depends on 72d9-8fbd (athletic-esthetical-polecat) landing first') and Acceptance Criteria (no sequencing gate AC)
scenarios: Agent implements container inheritance before 72d9-8ffd merges; containers now carry a non-empty dep set on a path where scoped sets are inert → attestations never invalidate on relevant file changes, silently passing the claim gate for drifted containers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one AC: 'The implementation MUST NOT be merged/activated before ticket 72d9-8fbd is confirmed merged; a guard or CI check enforces this.' Alternatively, add a defensive check in dependency_hashes that detects whether scoped dep support is active (e.g., by probing a known sentinel behavior of the attested path) and falls back to the pre-change behavior if not, with a logged warning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State why `dependency_hashes` is the right seam for child-union computation (e.g. 'keeps signing self-contained') OR note that the orchestrator should pre-compute the union using the already-loaded `PlanContext.children` (where full child `file_impact` is already in memory) and pass it through — avoiding N+1 redundant store reads on large epics.
evidence: orchestrator.py lines 200-215: 'fetch full child state (deps + file_impact) for P5/P8' — show_ticket already loads file_impact per child before signing
manifest.py dependency_hashes signature: `def dependency_hashes(verdict: dict[str, Any], *, repo_root=None)` — receives only the verdict dict, requiring fresh child reads inside it
Plan gives feasibility rationale ('same light store reads current_material_fingerprint uses') but no rationale for why this seam over the orchestrator where full child state is already in memory
On a large epic with many children, N+1 get_file_impact calls at signing time duplicates N+1 show_ticket calls already made in assemble_context
findings.finding: The plan places the child-union computation inside `dependency_hashes` (manifest.py), which means it must perform N+1 store reads (list_tickets + per-child get_file_impact) at signing time — but the orchestrator ALREADY fetches full child state including file_impact into PlanContext.children (via show_ticket, orchestrator.py lines 200-215) before signing begins. The plan gives no positive rationale for choosing this seam over using the already-assembled PlanContext.children, leaving an implementer likely to duplicate those reads unnecessarily.
findings.location: Approach §1 — 'dependency_hashes … child ids/statuses … child file_impact via rebar.get_file_impact'
scenarios: An epic with 20 children causes 20 extra get_file_impact reads at signing time, even though all 20 children's file_impact values were already fetched into PlanContext.children during assemble_context

An implementer following the plan literally writes a list_tickets + per-child get_file_impact loop inside dependency_hashes, missing the opportunity to use data already in the verdict or passed through as a parameter
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Approach §1: either 'the union is computed inside dependency_hashes (self-contained signing; reads are lightweight and fail-closed)' OR revise to 'pre-compute the union in the orchestrator from PlanContext.children (already fully fetched via show_ticket) and inject it into the verdict or pass it as a parameter to dependency_hashes, avoiding duplicate per-child reads.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify that child reads in `dependency_hashes` use `full=False` (or an equivalent lean read that fetches only `ticket_id` + `status`) rather than the default `full=True` body fetch, and confirm the N `get_file_impact` calls per non-closed child are within the acceptable latency envelope for the signing hot path.
evidence: Plan phrase: 'Child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads attest.current_material_fingerprint uses'
current_material_fingerprint (attest.py:751) calls _reads.list_tickets(parent=canonical) — list_tickets defaults to full=True, fetching description+comments per child
Plan separately adds 'child file_impact via rebar.get_file_impact' — one additional get_file_impact call per non-closed child on every dependency_hashes invocation
dependency_hashes is called at signing time (every review_plan that signs a manifest), so a container with 20 children incurs 21+ store reads per signing
findings.finding: The plan asserts child reads in dependency_hashes are 'light store reads' matching what current_material_fingerprint uses, but current_material_fingerprint calls list_tickets(parent=…) with full=True (the default), fetching full ticket bodies (description + comments) for every child; the plan then adds N additional rebar.get_file_impact calls on top. This makes dependency_hashes — called at every attestation signing — an N+1-read hot path for containers with many children, yet no read-cost qualification or full=False opt-in is specified.
findings.location: Approach §1 — 'Child ids/statuses come from the same light store reads attest.current_material_fingerprint uses; child file_impact via rebar.get_file_impact'
scenarios: A container epic with 15–30 children (common for large epics) triggers 15–30 get_file_impact + 1 list_tickets(full=True) on every plan-review signing, potentially adding significant latency to an otherwise fast local operation
If list_tickets is called with full=True, child descriptions + comments are deserialized and discarded — only status and ticket_id are actually needed by the poison rule
findings.suggested_fix: In the `dependency_hashes` child-union helper, call `_reads.list_tickets(parent=ticket_id, full=False)` to get only summary fields (status + ticket_id), then call `rebar.get_file_impact` only for non-closed children. Document the per-container O(N) read cost in the approach section so reviewers can evaluate it explicitly.
